page: Microsoft Azure F16als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 16 dedicated physical cores running 16 vCPUs at one thread per core, backed by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, establishing a compute-centric ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The underlying hardware incorporates support for advanced vector and cryptographic instructions, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware configurations exclude bundled local disks and discrete graphics hardware, requiring workloads to rely on remote Azure Premium Storage for persistent storage. Benchmark data reflects strong single-thread execution, with stress-ng single-core achieving 3080.57 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2097.0, both placing within the top 25%. Multi-core Geekbench reached 16815.0, supported by upper-quartile results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 209.64 GB/sec and image processing. Small-model LLM generation performed in the top 10% at 350.51 tokens per second, while general memory bandwidth, PassMark metrics, and static web serving throughput aligned with median tier distributions.

The 2:1 core-to-memory configuration delivers high CPU density per compute footprint, optimizing resource utilization for processing tasks that do not demand extensive RAM pools. Tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and absence of hardware GPU acceleration, requiring architectural offloading for high-IOPS local caching or large AI model training. The instance is suited for compute-heavy batch processing, code compilation, continuous integration, media transformation pipelines, and small-model inference tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F16als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine equipped with an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz across 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs. Configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, the instance maintains a 2.0 GB per core allocation tailored for CPU-intensive workloads rather than memory-heavy footprints. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support. No local storage or discrete GPUs are bundled, with disk operations handled via external Premium Storage. Benchmark results demonstrate upper-quartile execution in single-core stress testing, Geekbench scores, multi-threaded decompression, and small-model LLM inference, alongside mid-tier memory bandwidth and web serving. By avoiding excessive memory allocations and GPU hardware, the instance provides efficient computational density for CPU-bound tasks such as code compilation, media processing pipelines, and data compression workloads.
